CONTRACT v3: only `title` (<=6 words), `value`/figures, `note` (<=140 chars, partner-clean plain English), `status` (enum: market_priced | modeled | upside), and `fn` (footnote key) render — plus verbatim copy fields (headline/subline/lead/body/chips/cards). Underscore-prefixed fields NEVER reach the DOM. null/missing = render nothing. Footnotes render ONCE in a single 'Notes & assumptions' section above the contact form; a footnote's source_url may render as a small domain chip, never as a naked URL in body copy. Posture per AUTHORITY-MAP: ENABLE+BUILD — unlike Dubai/Abu Dhabi the authority is building marine transit, not operating it at scale (heritage abra line today, three corniche stations); the page posture is 'build the marine spine with the authority', with Navier as the fast zero-emission tier RAKTA's own Marine Transport Project scales into, resort corridors first. Emirate-internal corridors only — inter-emirate service is a later-phase roadmap item and is not rendered anywhere in this file. Disclosure rails: 'RAK Ports' is fine to name (the firewalled name is the Abu Dhabi three-letter ports group only); no royal-office references; Wynn Al Marjan is citable as a published development with sources. No counterparty identities, no program or fleet commitments, no launch dates (pipeline timing convention honored — RAKTA 2029 neither stated nor contradicted), no ridership claims (none primary-sourced).

fn1.text: Law No. 13 of 2023 on the licensing and operation of maritime means in Ras Al Khaimah designates the Ras Al Khaimah Transport Authority as the emirate's competent body for licensing, registering and operating marine vessels. Its Executive Regulation, announced 20 May 2026, governs vessel categories and operational controls, visiting-vessel licensing, the organization of marinas and berthing facilities, maritime training centers and events, safety, technical and environmental specifications, fees and penalties.

fn2.text: The authority's Marine Transport Project runs a scheduled heritage water line on the RAK Creek and Al Qawasim Corniche — stations at Qawasim Corniche 1, Qawasim Corniche 2 and Hilton Garden Inn — at AED 10 per station, with craft rental at AED 150 per 30 minutes and AED 300 per hour.

fn3.text: Visitor-economy figures from the Ras Al Khaimah Tourism Development Authority: a record 1.35 million overnight visitors in 2025 (+6%), tourism revenues up 12%, and published 2030 targets to exceed 3.5 million visitors a year and double the emirate's hotel keys.

fn4.text: FY2024 baseline per the tourism authority's published infographic: 1.284 million visitor arrivals (+5.1%), 71.2% hotel occupancy, an average daily rate of AED 592.5 (+14%), and an average stay of 3.52 days.

fn5.text: Ras Al Khaimah publishes no numeric waterway speed limits today. Every time on this page uses a conservative planning basis — slow near berths, in the creek and in the lagoons, 25 knots on the open coast, 20 knots after dark — and corridor distances are approximate, computed from real coordinates with over-water routing factors and rounded up. Final schedules are set with the authority under the 2026 Executive Regulation.

fn6.text: Wynn Al Marjan Island as published: a US$5.1 billion integrated resort of 1,530 rooms and suites with 22 dining and lounge venues, a theatre and a marina — the emirate's tallest structure, topped out at 283 metres in November 2025, opening 2027.

fn7.text: Landing status, stated plainly: Al Marjan Island has no public marine facility verified today and renders on interim-landing status until the published 2027 marina; Mina Al Arab's marina is developer-published. The foiling network uses four stops — Al Marjan, Al Hamra Royal Yacht Club, Mina Al Arab, and one Al Qawasim Corniche interchange. The authority's three Corniche abra stations remain as local heritage feeders to that interchange, not separate foiling terminals.

fn8.text: An authority modernizing every mode, per its own news pages: an agreement with Uber for smart taxi and limousine booking (April 2026), the emirate's first electric bus and a relaunched city route (June 2026), and a real-time passenger information system (2026).

gap.title: The authority is already on the water

copy.lead: Ras Al Khaimah is not starting from zero. The transport authority runs a scheduled heritage water line on the creek today, and in 2026 the emirate issued a complete marine licensing framework — expressly written to support investment, tourism and the growth of water transport on its waterways.
copy.support: The direction is written down: a single transport authority named the emirate's marine licensing body by law, a regulation that covers marinas and berthing facilities alongside safety and environmental specifications, and a destination strategy targeting more than 3.5 million visitors by 2030. A fast, zero-emission foiling spine is the network that framework was written for — built with the authority from the start, resort corridors first.

plans.note: A scheduled water line runs on the RAK Creek today — three corniche stations, published fares, the authority's own marine operation.
Law No. 13 of 2023 names the transport authority as the emirate's competent body for licensing and operating marine vessels.

plans.quote: …supports the investment environment in the maritime sector by providing a clear and stable regulatory framework that boosts investor confidence and supports the growth of maritime transport, tourism, and water sports activities.
plans.note: The authority's own frame for its new marine rules — investment-facing, tourism-facing, and written for operators.
An Uber agreement, the emirate's first electric bus and real-time passenger information — all in 2026. Marine is the natural next step.
1.35M visitors in 2025 and published targets of 3.5M+ by 2030 with double the hotel keys — the coast this spine serves.

copy.headline: No published limits yet. We plan conservatively.
copy.framing: Ras Al Khaimah publishes no numeric waterway speed limits today — its marine framework is new, and implementing rules may follow. Every time on this page uses a conservative planning basis: slow near berths and marine facilities, slower still in the creek shared with the heritage water line, careful in the lagoons, 25 knots only on the open coast, and 20 knots everywhere after dark. Final schedules are set with the authority.
copy.ask: In lagoon, creek and shoreline waters, the purpose of caution rules — wake, noise, disturbance — is served by a foiling electric vessel by design. What we offer the regulator is measurable: near-zero wake at speed, near-silent electric drive, and software-geofenced no-foil zones at every lagoon entrance and berth. Shown here only as what it offers — no allowance is assumed anywhere on this page.

expander.title: What conservative planning means here
body: The emirate's marine framework assigns speed and safety rule-making to the transport authority, and its 2026 Executive Regulation writes safety, technical and environmental specifications into licensing — but no numeric knot limits are published for RAK waters today. Rather than assume favorable numbers, every base time on this page is planned conservatively: berth collars and the heritage creek are treated as slow water, the lagoons as careful water, and after-dark running is capped, so evening times are shown longer, honestly.

When the authority writes its implementing rules, a foiling electric vessel serves the purpose behind wake and noise limits better than displacement hulls at the same speed — near-zero wake foilborne, near-silent drive, geofenced no-foil zones at lagoon entrances and berths. That is offered as evidence for the rule-making conversation, never as a schedule assumption: no relief is priced or timed anywhere on this page.

rule_basis.detail: 5 kn within 50 m of shore/facilities · 8 kn full RAK Creek (stricter than the AD channel tier on purpose — shared with abras and moored dhows) · 12 kn lagoon/breakwater approaches · 25 kn open coast (N45 service speed, vessel-capability bound) · 20 kn night. Mirrors Abu Dhabi Maritime's codified tiers as the nearest UAE analog; NOT presented as RAK rules anywhere — the renderable copy says 'planning basis' and names no foreign instrument.

RAKTA designated competent body; regulation covers maritime safety requirements, technical and environmental specifications; rak.ae legislation text includes an operator duty 'not to exceed speed limits in maritime routes' (numeric values not published in the English text located)

navier_intro.title: Meet the vessel

copy.headline: Zero-emission. Near-silent. Almost no wake.
copy.subline: Navier is a U.S. builder of electric hydrofoil vessels — the traits that matter for harbor rules and harbor neighbors are built into the hull, not bolted on.
copy.body: The N45 Explorer carries 20 passengers at a foilborne cruise speed of about 20 knots, lifted clear of the water for a smooth, wake-free ride. The smaller N30 Quanta carries 8. Foiling cuts energy use by up to ~90% versus a conventional planing hull, and both vessels run near-silent on electric power.

reference.title: Reference

copy.intro: Ras Al Khaimah's water-transport landscape is compact and clearly mandated. We seek conversations — nothing here implies approval, endorsement, or commitment by any body named.

bodies.role: The emirate's sole transport authority — roads, public transport and marine. Named the competent body for marine licensing and operation by Law 13 of 2023, it runs the heritage water line today and organizes marinas and berthing under the 2026 Executive Regulation. The primary counterpart for the marine spine.

The emirate's commercial ports group, with the harbor-master function inside port limits under Act No. 9 of 2008 — pilotage, conduct and speed in port waters. The network's corridors run outside port limits; coordination applies only if a corridor ever calls at a port.
Municipal land, beaches and the waterfront public realm — landing-side approvals for shoreline structures outside port and marina estates.

Destination strategy and data — a record 1.35 million visitors in 2025 and published targets to exceed 3.5 million and double hotel keys by 2030. The demand-side sponsor of the tourism-weighted corridors on this network.
Government-owned master developer of Al Marjan Island and the Marjan Beach masterplan — the gatekeeper for island landings until the published 2027 marina opens.
